title: Structural Identity

story.briefing: Two survey teams mapped the same lattice independently. If their maps differ anywhere at all, one of them walked the wrong section.
story.success: Maps agree. Both surveys are accepted.

description: Given two binary trees, return true if they have exactly the same shape and the same value at every corresponding position, and false otherwise. Two empty trees are identical. A tree is given as an array where the node at index i has its left child at index 2i+1 and its right child at index 2i+2. A null entry means there is no node there, and nothing exists beneath it. An empty array is an empty tree.
hints: Two trees match if their roots match and both pairs of subtrees match. Same recursive shape as the traversals, with two indices moving together.
The arrays can have different lengths and still describe the same tree, because trailing nulls are not significant. Compare the trees, not the arrays.

Write a helper on one index used for both trees. Treat out-of-range or null as absent. Return true if both are absent, false if only one is, and otherwise compare the values and recurse into both children.
